root_idea.summary: A root oriented toward persistent attachment, insistence, and the pressure of an obligation.
root_idea.development: From the idea of clinging or pressing upon someone, the root develops into creditor–debtor relations, financial liabilities and losses, and punishment or affliction that remains attached. This root-level development does not make every derivative a direct synonym of every other derivative.

senses.definition: A person burdened by debt or a financial obligation.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic category al-ghārimīn, the term denotes indebted persons rather than the debt or liability itself.

senses.definition: An affliction, punishment, or perdition that clings persistently and is not escaped.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression at 25:65, the word describes an abiding torment or calamity; the attested interpretations include persistent evil, hardship, severe punishment, and perdition.

senses.definition: Burdened with debt or made to incur a financial loss.
senses.usage_conditions: The passive participle presents a person as subjected to a financial burden, whether rendered as laden with debt or as having been made to suffer loss.

senses.definition: A financial loss, damage, or detriment borne in property without wrongdoing.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic use at 9:98, the word denotes expenditure or a financial outlay regarded as a loss.

senses.definition: A debt or financial obligation that must be paid or borne.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic uses at 52:40 and 68:46, the word denotes an incurred financial burden or liability, including an obligation imposed or undertaken rather than freely chosen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pay or discharge an obligatory payment, bloodwit, responsibility, or similar liability; also, to take responsibility for paying it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The liability may already be incumbent on the person or, in some usages, may be one that he undertakes himself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suffer a loss in trade.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A commercial usage contrasted with gaining profit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone pay or discharge a due payment, or to make someone incur a debt, fine, or other obligation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative construction governing the person made liable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of clouds, to discharge rain or water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or tropical usage describing clouds as made to discharge what they hold.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render someone eagerly desirous, fond of, or attached to a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may be followed by بِـ to mark the object of attachment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take upon oneself an obligation, such as payment of a fine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reflexive construction describing voluntary assumption of financial liability.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The self-imposition of a financial burden, difficulty, damage, or loss, including giving property against one's will.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun focuses on assuming what is termed غرامة or otherwise becoming subject to its hardship.
A broader Classical Arabic application of the payment or liability branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who is heavy or sluggish.
A woman who is angry, estranged, or has broken off relations with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An alternative lexical interpretation of the same headword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An oath word meaning verily, surely, or now indeed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in an oath expression such as غَرْمَى وَجَدِّكَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Eager desire, fondness, or attachment, especially love that torments the heart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the desire or attachment branch, distinct from the Quranic sense of persistent punishment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A debtor, one who is obliged to pay a debt, bloodwit, or similar liability.
A creditor, one to whom a debt is owed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an established opposite use of the same relational noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An adversary, antagonist, or litigant in a dispute.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense develops from the creditor's pressing or clinging to the debtor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A captive of love, or one to whom love clings; eagerly desirous of or attached to a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may describe attachment to women or persistent fondness for an object.

cautions: The related noun غَرِيمٌ is used in Classical Arabic for both debtor and creditor. The Quranic غَارِمِينَ entry is presented in the indebted sense supported by the Quran-focused discussion; the creditor sense is kept separately as Classical Arabic evidence.
